An $800B market. A once-in-a-generation technology shift. This is the moment. This is the team. Come build something generational with us.

paras: You are the storyteller for Agentio's product. You take the facts, stats and launch briefs the product marketing team produces and turn them into the words, decks and one-pagers brands and our GTM team use every day. If a customer has an aha moment reading our pitch, you wrote the sentence.

ashby:alchemy:b6b29a64-508c-4712-9b0f-08.summary:
Alchemy is the Web3 infrastructure and developer platform that powers millions of users and the world’s most innovative blockchain applications. From enabling $1+ trillion in financial transactions worldwide to scaling L2s and enabling DeFi, Alchemy provides the infrastructure and tools developers need to build reliable, scalable, and accessible experiences.

Trusted by companies like JPMorgan, Stripe, Visa, Franklin Templeton, Nike, and backed by a16z, Coatue, Silver Lake, Lightspeed, and Stanford University, Alchemy is building the foundational layer for a decentralized and AI-enabled Web3 ecosystem. For more information, visit alchemy.com .

sections.title: About the role
paras: Self-serve is how Alchemy grows. The dashboard and the developer experience around it are the primary revenue engine for our flagship products: developers discover us, sign up, get to their first call, scale their usage, and upgrade largely without ever talking to a person. That funnel is one of the most direct levers on company-level revenue we have, and this role owns it.

It's also changing fast. A growing share of developers now reach Alchemy through an AI coding agent rather than a browser tab, and we expect agent-mediated usage to become the dominant way our platform is consumed. Building for that shift, our MCP server, agent skills, and AI-native onboarding, sits squarely in this role.

You'll run the dashboard as a product, own the self-serve growth engine, and set the experimentation and measurement standard for growth across the company, partnering with Node APIs, Data APIs, Wallets, Transaction Engine, Growth Marketing, and Billing, and spending meaningful time with customers.

sections.title: What you'll own
bullets: The dashboard. Own signup, app creation, first key, first call, usage and CU visibility, upgrade paths, team management, and the observability developers need to debug their own traffic.

Developer experience end to end. Docs, SDKs, quickstarts, error messages, sandbox and testnet flows, and the first hour of every integration. Reduce time to first successful call, then time to first paid workload.
Own product-led growth end to end. Design the developer journey from docs, to first API call, to first paid workload, to scaled production spend. Instrument it, find the drop-offs, fix them.

Agent experience (AX). Make Alchemy the default infrastructure an AI coding agent reaches for. Own how our MCP server, agent skills, and machine readable docs perform inside Claude Code, Cursor, and whatever comes next.
Experimentation. Building the A/B and holdout tooling, running pricing, packaging, and onboarding tests, and creating a habit of shipping and learning weekly rather than quarterly.
Proven product-led growth leadership : you've owned a self-serve funnel at scale and can show what you moved, by how much, and how you know it was you.
Rigorous experimentation practice. You know the difference between a lift and a fluke, you size tests before you run them, and you've built the culture as much as the tooling.
Genuinely analytical. Data Analysis is a normal Tuesday. You can build the model, audit the instrumentation, catch the bad join, and defend the number in front of the exec team.

Artificial Analysis is the leading independent AI benchmarking company. We support labs, engineers and enterprises to understand AI capabilities and make critical decisions about their AI strategies. Our benchmarks don’t just measure the cutting edge of AI, they are actively shaping the frontier.

paras: AI hardware is where the next decade of AI economics will be decided, and our hardware benchmarks are becoming the reference point for how the industry measures accelerators. We’re hiring into our hardware pillar to drive that coverage: benchmarking the GPUs, TPUs and custom silicon the AI industry runs on, and building the analysis that helps the industry understand them.

You’ll design and run performance benchmarks across accelerators and inference configurations, extend our hardware benchmarking stack, including AA-AgentPerf and our performance benchmarking suite, build cost and throughput models, and work directly with the leading chipmakers to benchmark their latest silicon. paras: • Benchmark AI Accelerators: Design and execute performance benchmarking across GPUs, TPUs and custom inference silicon, measuring throughput, latency and price-performance the way the industry actually deploys

• Build Evaluation Methodology: Develop and maintain the frameworks that define how AI hardware performance and efficiency are measured, extending products like AA-AgentPerf, from tokens per second and time-to-first-token to total cost of ownership

• Analyze Inference Economics: Deeply understand how cost-per-token, utilization and hardware choice interact, and translate that into analysis the industry relies on for deployment and procurement decisions

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Commure Ambient is our Ambient AI platform. A clinician records the visit, and a finished note lands in their EHR, along with ICD codes, orders, a Patient 360 summary, and carried-forward history on supported systems. For a physician, that means charting is done when the visit is done.

Practices decide on Ambient by trying it: their own providers, their own patients, inside their own EHR. As a Sales Engineer on the Ambient team, you'll own those pilots from the first scoping call through a signed contract and hand-off to implementation.

This is a presales role. You'll partner with Account Executives on Commure Ambient pilots and on advanced AI pilots with healthcare practices: coding, orders, Patient 360, carry forward, and pre-visit summaries, running live inside ten EHRs (athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, AdvancedMD, ModMed, NextGen, Practice Fusion, WebPT, Prompt, iKnowMed, and Meditech Expanse). You'll typically have several pilots in flight at once, and you'll work closely with Engineering, our template team, and our implementation and operations teams to make each one succeed.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Scope pilots. Lead the technical scoping call for each pilot, working directly with the providers who'll use Ambient and the decision makers evaluating it. Capture specialty, note types, EHR, and workflow, and turn it into a technical scope the deal can move forward on.

Build EHR integrations. Stand up the integration for each pilot across browser automation, DOM injection, and API paths. Our target from approved requests to a live integration the customer can use. When a note doesn't land in the chart, you'll find out why and fix it.

Bring advanced AI into the pilot. Confirm which beyond-the-note features the customer's EHR supports, configure them, and help providers put them to work: ICD coding, orders, Patient 360, carry forward, and pre-visit summaries.
Get templates right. Translate gold-standard notes and specialty requirements into template requests for our template engineering team, and triage template updates during the pilot on a 24-hour SLA.

ashby:morpho:8d24e3a6-a509-48d8-bc17-089.summary: Morpho is a leading Decentralized Finance (DeFi) lending protocol backed by a16z crypto, Paradigm, Ribbit Capital, Apollo, Vaneck, Coinbase Ventures, Variant and 50 others to build an open credit network giving anyone, anywhere, access to the best possible terms. Morpho is experiencing exponential adoption, with over billion in deposits on the network and used by institutional clients including Bitwise, Galaxy, and Anchorage Digital and the largest crypto exchanges, such as Coinbase, Binance, and Kraken. Now, Morpho is scaling its team of contributors to establish itself as the open credit network, not just of DeFi, but of the world.

sections.title: Why Morpho Exists
paras: Everyone has the potential to build something great for the world. But fulfilling that ambition almost always requires more: people willing to trust you with their capital. Yet access to capital still depends on where you live, who you know, and which institutions are willing to trust you. Even when capital is available, it sits fragmented across disconnected networks and hidden behind intermediaries. The result is a system that fails most of the people it should serve. Borrowers overpay. Lenders earn less than they should. Many are shut out entirely, not because they are unworthy of credit, but because today's infrastructure was never built to connect them. Morpho exists to solve this. Full article here .

Track product data to identify growth levers, such as rolling products out to new jurisdictions or running activation campaigns, and turn them into quantified expansion plays

sections.title: Role

Morpho provides open credit infrastructure that payments companies can build on. This role leads that work: you will partner with acquirers, card issuers, payment networks and lenders to understand what they need, and shape Morpho's infrastructure so their products can put credit to use.

sections.title: Responsibilities

Prioritize market opportunities across networks, partner types, and regions, and make the trade-offs explicit.

Create scalable products and integrations that any acquirer, issuer or lender can adopt, and make the build or partner call for each piece.
Work as a peer to the protocol team on design trade-offs, such as how settlement data is verified and how lenders are repaid, bringing legal in early on requirements by jurisdiction.

paras: You understand Morpho's lending stack, Midnight and the current receivables build in detail: who the partners are, how money and data move, and where it breaks. You have met protocol, solutions, partnerships and legal, and spoken with the current partners yourself.

Version one is written down: standard terms, the integration path and what lenders require. You have tested it with several acquirers or issuers and more than one lender, and the first partner is onboarding on those terms. You have a ranked map of the wider payments opportunity.

Loans repeat every week, with more than one borrower and more than one lender on standard terms. A second use case, on the issuer side or a second network, is in proof of concept. Morpho has the evidence to decide how much further to invest in payments.

greenhouse:celonis:8002804003.summary: Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

sections.title: The Team
paras: The Client Director is a senior member of our sales organization, responsible for the long-arc commercial trajectory of Celonis’s most strategically important accounts. You sit at the intersection of enterprise sales leadership and platform strategy—owning a focused portfolio of one to few large accounts generating significant ARR, and working in close partnership with Value Engineers, Client Value Partners (CVP), and Professional Services to grow, protect, and compound that revenue over multi-year horizons.

sections.title: The Role
paras: As the Client Director for a Strategic Life Sciences Account, your primary objective is to develop, maintain, and expand resilient sponsorship and sticky business critical use cases across the client’s business. You are accountable for moving accounts from solving individual pain points to an Enterprise AI platform of record—embedding the Celonis platform as a strategic pillar within the client’s operations.

You are the client’s most senior commercial partner, engaging at the C-suite level on business strategy, platform investment, and multi-year transformation. Where a CVP is deployed, you own the commercial relationship and expansion strategy; they own value realization and adoption.

sections.title: The work you’ll do
bullets: Own the commercial relationship: Serve as the primary executive point of contact across the C-suite—CEO, CFO, CSCO, COO, CIO—building relationships that transcend any individual deal cycle and anchor Celonis to the customer’s long-term strategic agenda.

Drive ARR and NRR growth: Develop and execute a structured expansion roadmap—identifying new business units, geographies, use cases, and platform capabilities that compound ARR over time. Lead commercial negotiations for expansions, renewals, and multi-year enterprise agreements in partnership with Deal Desk and Legal.

Translate adoption into commercial momentum: Partner with the CVP and Value Engineering teams to convert adoption milestones and realized value into renewal confidence and expansion urgency. Own executive business reviews that are forward-looking and commercially anchored.

Embed Celonis as a strategic platform: Position Celonis within the customer's AI strategy—connecting Process Intelligence to their LLM, automation, and agentic AI investments so the platform becomes a foundational data and orchestration layer, not a point solution.

Protect through transformation: Proactively identify and mitigate commercial risk: sponsor departures, competitive displacement, implementation fatigue, and budget consolidation. Ensure multi-threaded executive relationships and a documented value story that survives the leadership transitions common in large enterprise accounts.

Scale the practice: Codify account strategies, expansion motions, and transformation navigation approaches into reusable assets for the broader Strategic Accounts practice. Maintain disciplined account plan, pipeline strategy and coverage to any growth targets, and forecast accuracy across a small, complex account set.

sections.title: The qualifications you need
paras: Visa sponsorship is not offered for this role.
bullets: 12+ years in enterprise SaaS sales or strategic account management, with at least 5 years managing accounts with $5M+ ARR.
Deep industry expertise in Life Sciences— with the credibility to engage customers on industry-specific challenges, benchmarks, and transformation priorities, not just platform capabilities.
Preferred direct experience with Life Sciences accounts, leading transformation initiatives or acting as a strategic consultant or Client Director.
Demonstrated track record of growing ARR within named accounts over multi-year horizons—expanding platform footprint, not just renewing contracts.
Executive presence and credibility at the C-suite level—able to lead strategic conversations with CFOs, COOs, and CIOs and influence large, complex buying decisions.
Experience navigating enterprise transformations—ERP consolidations, cloud migrations, M&A, organizational restructuring—without losing commercial momentum.
Fluent in business case construction: ROI modeling, TCO analysis, and value benchmarking at a level that withstands CFO scrutiny.
Comfortable with long deal cycles and ambiguity; skilled at managing internal and external stakeholders across 12–24+ month expansion arcs.

greenhouse:cottonwoodresidential:6241573.summary:
Cottonwood Residential is a forward-thinking, fully integrated real estate company focused on the multifamily sector. We combine deep expertise in asset and property management with a commitment to operational excellence across a growing national portfolio. We don’t just manage communities — we elevate them.

The Customer Experience Specialist plays a key role in delivering an elevated living experience across Cottonwood Residential communities. As the first point of contact for prospects, residents, and vendors, this individual sets the tone for every interaction and ensures each customer feels welcomed, supported, and valued. This role is ideal for a service-driven professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment, excels at building relationships, and takes pride in creating a seamless and memorable customer journey, from first impression through daily resident interactions.

sections.title: Customer Experience & Front Office Operations
bullets: Serve as the first point of contact for all customers, including prospects, residents, and vendors
Create a welcoming office environment by greeting every visitor with professionalism and positivity
Deliver exceptional customer service by identifying needs and providing timely, effective solutions
Answer and manage all incoming calls, documenting detailed and accurate information in property management systems
Assist residents with requests such as package retrieval, key distribution, work order entry, and general inquiries
Act as a liaison between residents and maintenance teams to ensure service requests are handled efficiently

sections.title: Leasing Support & Sales
bullets: Maintain up-to-date knowledge of apartment availability, pricing, and community features
Support leasing efforts by answering prospect questions and assisting with the application and documentation process
Conduct follow-up communication with prospective residents to support conversion and occupancy goals
Prepare apartment homes for move-ins and assist with move-in and move-out processes

sections.title: Community Presentation & Operations
bullets: Walk the community regularly to ensure amenities, buildings, and tour paths meet Cottonwood standards
Open, close, and maintain Self-Guided Tour units, ensuring cleanliness and readiness at all times
Assist with signage, directional materials, and overall tour experience setup
Maintain knowledge of the local area to better assist prospects and residents

sections.title: Marketing & Resident Engagement
paras: We don’t just manage properties — we elevate them. At Cottonwood Residential, you’ll join a culture that values innovation, collaboration, and operational excellence. You’ll work alongside a team that is passionate about delivering exceptional living experiences while supporting your professional growth. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package and opportunities to grow within a dynamic, expanding organization.

Cottonwood Residential uses AI-assisted technology and authorized recruiting partners to support our hiring process. By applying, you acknowledge that you may communicate with AI-powered systems during scheduling, candidate outreach, or preliminary interviews, and that interviews may be recorded, transcribed, and summarized for evaluation by our hiring team.
By applying, you consent to receiving communications regarding your application by phone, text message, email, or other electronic means. Hiring decisions are solely made by Cottonwood Residential.
bullets: Support community marketing efforts, including social media posting and outreach initiatives
Assist in planning and executing resident events and engagement activities
Contribute to building a strong community atmosphere that enhances resident satisfaction and retention
High school diploma or GED required
1+ years of in-person, customer facing experience required
1+ years of other customer service, administrative, sales, or hospitality experience required
Multifamily property management experience is a plus
Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to engage professionally with a wide range of audiences

greenhouse:cultureamp:8351331.summary: We’re big believers in the power of IRL, so for most roles we ask Campers to work from their local Culture Amp office an average of 2 days a week to unlock connection, pace and culture together.

sections.title: Join us on our mission to make a better world of work.
paras: Culture Amp is the world’s leading employee experience platform, revolutionizing how 25 million employees across more than 6,000 companies create a better world of work. Culture Amp empowers companies of all sizes and industries to transform employee engagement, drive performance management, and develop high-performing teams. Powered by people science and the most comprehensive employee dataset in the world, the most innovative companies including Canva, On, Asana, Dolby, McDonalds and Nasdaq depend on Culture Amp every day.

Culture Amp is backed by leading venture capital funds and has offices in the US, UK, Germany and Australia. Culture Amp has been recognized as one of the world’s top private cloud companies by Forbes and most innovative companies by Fast Company.
For more information visit cultureamp.com .

sections.title: How you can help make a better world of work
paras: Culture Amp is looking for a Director, Solutions Engineering to lead our Solutions Engineering team within Customer Value & Services. You’ll set the strategy, operating rhythm and standards for the technical team that helps customers understand and realise the value of Culture Amp, from first conversation through to a strong start.

You’ll balance building the team with staying close to the field. That means joining key customer conversations, coaching on complex multi-stakeholder deals and levelling up how the team discovers, demonstrates and solves. You’ll work closely with Sales, Customer Experience, Product and People Science, including the 'pods' that share ownership of the customer from first sale through to renewal, and bring what customers tell you back into how we sell and build. You’ll also lead a team that uses AI to do better work, not just faster work.

sections.title: You will
bullets: Lead, coach and develop your Solutions Engineers through regular 1:1s, clear feedback, performance conversations and career paths, and hire people who bring both the right skills and the right values.
Set the vision for Solutions Engineering and turn it into an operating rhythm: coverage, priorities, forecasting input and performance measures that surface problems early.

Stay close to the field by joining key customer meetings, guiding technical discovery and validation on complex deals, and coaching the team to tailor solutions to what a customer’s people and business really need.
Raise the standard of demos and value-led storytelling, so your team can explain technical complexity clearly to People, IT and executive stakeholders.

Line up pre-sales and post-sales so that what’s agreed in the sales cycle carries through to a smooth start, with clean handoffs and shared account context, and a focus on shorter time to value and stronger retention.
Build assets that scale, such as frameworks, playbooks, onboarding plans and enablement, so good practice reaches the wider team and doesn’t depend on one person.
Partner with leaders across Sales, Customer Experience, Product, People Science, RevOps and GTM Enablement to improve win rates, deal quality and adoption.
Turn customer feedback and patterns from the field into clear, evidence-backed input for Product and roadmap decisions.

sections.title: You have
bullets: 8+ years in solutions engineering, pre-sales or technical consulting in B2B SaaS, including 4+ years leading Solutions Engineering teams.
A track record of building, scaling and developing teams, with people who’ve grown into stronger SEs and leaders under you.
Credibility leading discovery, technical validation and demos across complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales cycles, including security, integration and RFP questions.
Experience building scalable frameworks, playbooks and enablement that other teams actually use.
Fluency with Salesforce, Gong or equivalents, and the discipline to use data to forecast, prioritise and measure.
Hands-on experience using AI tools in your own work, and experience getting a team to build AI-enabled habits.
Examples of cross-functional work that moved metrics such as win rate, time to value or retention, where influence mattered more than authority.
Executive presence and the ability to connect product capability to meaningful outcomes for senior HR and business leaders.

greenhouse:dashlane:8352606.summary:
Dashlane’s mission is to deliver the credential security every business and employee needs to thrive. Millions of consumers, and over 25,000 brands worldwide, such as Michelin, Air France, and Forrester, trust Dashlane for industry-leading innovations, patented zero-knowledge security, and an unmatched user experience. Founded in Paris, Dashlane has since established offices in New York and Lisbon, and has grown to more than 300 Dashlaners globally.

We're looking for people who actively use AI tools to drive efficiency, creativity, and impact in their work. At Dashlane, we drive innovation and value learning, strive for excellence in everything we do, and thrive as one team. Learn more about life at Dashlane , including how we work , how we hire , and the benefits of being a Dashlaner .

sections.title: About the role
paras: As our Staff Product Manager for Agentic Capabilities, you will own the vision, strategy and roadmap for how Dashlane becomes an interface for AI agents and assistants for consumers and businesses. Success means people hand real, valuable tasks to agents through Dashlane and keep doing it, and companies trust it enough to let their teams do the same.

You will own the product alongside senior engineers as a Staff-level individual contributor in a 0-to-1 role where standards are still unsettled. We are looking for strong familiarity with the modern AI landscape, including LLMs, assistants and agentic workflows, and sound judgment about what agents can and cannot be trusted with.

At Dashlane, we embrace a hybrid culture that combines the best of both worlds: the creativity and energy of in-person collaboration with the flexibility of remote work. Our model is designed to strengthen team connections while supporting individual productivity and work-life balance. To maximize collaboration, we come together in the office on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays, while Wednesdays and Fridays offer more flexibility for focused work.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Set the direction. Form and defend a point of view on how agents and assistants should act with what Dashlane protects, for consumers and businesses, and turn it into a strategy, positioning, and multi-year plan that leadership will back.

Read the market and judge readiness. Keep a living view of how agent makers, assistants, browsers, identity vendors and password managers are moving. Assess how ready emerging pieces such as passkeys for agents and agent sign-in standards are, and set the triggers for acting on each.
Own the evidence. Run discovery on the jobs people hand to agents at home and at work. Establish who hands over real tasks and what holds them back, so your bets follow demand, not hype.

Connect consumer and business. Treat both as a connected problem. Turn what we learn from individuals handing tasks to agents into the visibility and controls that IT and Security teams need to govern agent access at work. Flag when a decision for one audience affects the other.

Own the trust commitment. Define what Dashlane promises about what an agent or model can see and do, and hold every product decision and release to that promise. Turn what agents can and cannot be trusted with into a set of durable product primitives, such as limits, approvals, records and revocation, that stay valid as agents change.

Own the numbers. Set baselines and targets for adoption, repeat use and trust, including time to a first approved agent login, how long people take to decide on an agent’s request, and how often failures are recovered without the person starting over. Be accountable for them to leadership.

Align the organization. Bring Design, Engineering, Security, Legal, Sales & Marketing towards one plan, establish the operating rhythm and decision framework for the team, and settle ownership where it is unclear.

sections.title: In your first year:
bullets: By 90 days, the team's early engineering work has become a shared view of the problem, a trust model that Security and Architecture back, and proposed targets for what "working" means. You have shared a point of view on the category with Dashlane leadership.
By 6 months, real people are experiencing agentic value through Dashlane, engagement is recurring, and you know who gets the most value first.

By 12 months, people keep using it and it shows in who chooses and stays on our plans. A version for companies has a clear first slice, and you have a view on where to go next. You have a vision and roadmap for agents and assistants across B2B and B2C that leadership has backed.

sections.title: Requirements
bullets: 8+ years in product management, including ownership of an authentication, security, identity or permissions-heavy product, and at least one product you took from zero to market with measurable success (adoption, revenue or retention) in a market that was still emerging.

Enough technical fluency (OAuth, passkeys, sessions, browser extensions) to follow a token-flow discussion with engineers and ask where it breaks. You don't need to write code but you must be comfortable with speaking the language of engineering.
A track record of reading a fast-moving market and turning its signals into a strategy that leadership acted on.
Experience running 0-to-1 discovery with small samples and incomplete information, defining success as customer outcomes rather than shipped features.

AI-native ways of working: you build working prototypes with AI, run discovery synthesis through it, chain agents into your own workflow, and can show concretely how it has changed how you “do product”.
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English: crisp problem statements, clear 1-pagers, compelling roadmap rationale, and external narratives that shape how a category is understood.

greenhouse:databricks:8548502002.summary:
The Field Engineering role is changing quickly. AI is changing how technical work gets done, products and customer needs are evolving faster, and the capabilities that distinguish an exceptional FE today will not be exactly the same ones that matter tomorrow.

Databricks is looking for a Lead Technical Enablement Specialist to help define and build the capability engine for our global Field Engineering organization. You will shape how FEs build expertise, demonstrate readiness, share what they know, and apply their capabilities with customers.

This role owns a portfolio, not a single program. That portfolio may include skills verification, technical validation, role-based readiness paths, practical challenges, and new approaches we have not yet imagined. Your job is to understand where the field is headed, identify the capabilities that will matter most, and turn that insight into…

sections.title: About the Role
paras: This is a high-visibility, high-autonomy role for someone who wants to build. You will work with FE leaders, product and technical communities, regional teams, enablement partners, HR, and internal platform teams to define what “field-ready” means and make it useful in the flow of work. You will have the opportunity to influence how a global technical organization develops - and to create programs that become part of how Databricks operates.

The best person for this role is equal parts strategist, product thinker, builder, and operator. You can see around corners, create structure from ambiguity, earn trust with senior stakeholders, and turn an idea into something the field actually uses. You are energized by the possibility of using AI not only as a topic to teach, but as a catalyst to redesign how capability is built, measured, and scaled.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Set the vision and roadmap for FE capability. Develop a clear point of view on how Databricks should build, demonstrate, recognize, and continuously evolve field expertise. Translate FE strategy, product priorities, customer needs, and the changing nature of technical work into a focused portfolio of investments.

Own and evolve a portfolio of readiness experiences. Bring together existing programs and new opportunities across skills verification, technical demonstrations, role-based pathways, credentials, and practical application. Decide what to scale, redesign, connect, or retire to keep the portfolio coherent and valuable.

Create the systems and signals that make capability visible. Partner with internal platform and engineering teams to turn program concepts into simple, scalable experiences. Ensure that skills, evidence, readiness milestones, and development recommendations are useful to FEs, managers, and leaders in the systems they already use.

Build the operating model for a federated technical organization. Establish clear ownership, governance, quality standards, content and assessment lifecycles, and feedback loops across global programs, product SMEs, regional leaders, and enablement partners. Create mechanisms that let expertise scale without centralizing every decision.

Drive adoption through influence and strong field experience. Build the narrative, stakeholder plan, manager engagement, and operating rhythm needed to make programs matter. Listen carefully to the field, remove friction, and use adoption data and qualitative feedback to improve the experience.

Give leaders a clear view of capability and opportunity. Define meaningful measures of participation, proficiency, capability coverage, readiness, and emerging gaps. Use data to help leaders decide where to invest, where to raise the bar, and how the FE organization is evolving.

Connect capability to growth and career opportunities. Partner with FE leadership, HR, and career architecture owners to make demonstrated capability useful in development conversations, specialization paths, succession planning, and career progression where appropriate.

sections.title: What Success Looks Like
bullets: Established a compelling, shared point of view on what FE capability and readiness need to look like in an AI-enabled Databricks.
Created a clear roadmap for the field capability portfolio, with explicit priorities and decisions about what to scale, improve, or stop.
Launched or materially evolved high-value readiness experiences that FEs and managers see as relevant to their work - not administrative requirements.
Built strong partnerships across FE leadership, product and technical communities, regional teams, HR, and internal platform teams.
Given leaders and managers better visibility into capability, gaps, and trends - and helped them act on those signals.
Established a scalable operating model that enables expertise to grow across the organization without creating unnecessary central processes.
Demonstrated measurable progress in adoption, capability coverage, field confidence, or other outcomes that matter to the business.

sections.title: What We're Looking For
bullets: 6+ years of experience in technical enablement, product management, learning and development, consulting, field engineering, or program leadership within a high-growth technology company.
A track record of building and scaling something new from ambiguity. You have shaped the strategy, aligned stakeholders, designed the experience, launched it, measured it, and improved it over time.

Strong strategic judgment and executive presence. You can partner with Directors and VPs to shape priorities, make tradeoffs, challenge assumptions constructively, and turn a broad vision into clear decisions.
A product mindset. You start with the user and the problem, test assumptions, design for adoption, and continuously improve the experience based on evidence.
The ability to balance rigor with practicality. You know how to create credible standards and meaningful signals without adding unnecessary friction for the field.
Strong data fluency. You can define useful measures, interpret dashboards, identify patterns, and use data and field feedback to drive decisions.
Experience partnering with internal product, engineering, or platform teams to turn program requirements into scalable tools and workflows.

Genuine curiosity about AI and its impact on technical work, customer engagement, and organizational capability. Hands-on experience using AI to improve assessment, personalization, content, or operations is a plus.

greenhouse:dept:8352418.summary:
We are a Growth Invention company built to help the world’s most ambitious brands grow faster. Operating at the intersection of technology and marketing, we create what is next by pioneering ideas, acting fast, and moving further because standing still just is not in our DNA.

We are drawn to people who stay curious, move with intent, and never stop inventing. Our culture runs on three values: better together, relentlessly curious, and get sh*t done. It is how we work, how we grow, and how we make things that matter.

At DEPT®, you will find the freedom to explore, the space to collaborate, and the trust to make a real impact for our clients, for each other, and for the world we are helping to build.

sections.title: THE ROLE:
paras: The Director, Social role is ultimately responsible for building and managing a high-performing team that handles Strategy, Planning, and Activation to best service their clients. Their top priorities are strong client growth/retention and employee growth/retention.

The Director, Social should be able to lead the team to deliver excellent paid social strategy and performance recommendations for their clients based on DEPT’s best practices. They are effective communicators who can inspire and motivate teams to achieve and exceed client goals based on their deep understanding of the ins and outs of their clients’ businesses and they proactively bring innovative strategy, holistic ideas, and leadership to help clients meet their overarching business goals.
Reports to: Group Director, Client Partnership

sections.title: WHAT YOU’LL DO:
bullets: Develop the social expertise of your direct reports, providing mentorship, feedback and coaching on paid social best practices
Maintaining a strong understanding of the holistic business for each client in their portfolio
Orchestrate collaboration and implementation for flawless execution of paid social campaign strategy, planning and activation

The C&M platform acts as the central nervous system between our content creation (Spark CMS) and our downstream consumers—powering FT.com, our mobile apps, Specialist publications, B2B syndication, and new AI-driven experiences.

This is a senior Individual Contributor (IC) role that requires deep technical curiosity and domain expertise. You will not have direct reports; instead, you will partner closely with a Principal Engineer and three Tech Leads, collectively guiding the product vision for an execution team of 12-13 engineers. You will also collaborate extensively across FT Core (specifically Access & Identity), Editorial Tech, Data Science, Commercial (B2B), Editorial, and Legal to ensure our metadata and content pipelines serve diverse and complex needs.

sections.title: What You Will Do
bullets: Drive Platform Strategy: Co-create and champion the product roadmap for the Content & Metadata platform in partnership with engineering leadership, ensuring FT journalism is treated as a highly structured, reusable, and discoverable asset.

Your deep understanding of content platforms, API-driven architectures, document stores (MongoDB), and graph databases (Neo4j) will be critical in making collaborative architectural tradeoffs and earning the team's trust.

Shape Knowledge Management & Ontologies: Collaborate to guide the evolution of the FT’s Knowledge Graph, helping ensure content is semantically segmented, enriched with accurate metadata, and connected to power advanced search and AI use cases.

Stakeholder Alignment: Act as the bridge between highly technical engineering teams and cross-functional business stakeholders, translating B2B commercial goals, editorial requirements, and legal compliance into actionable, shared technical goals.

sections.title: Key Focus Areas & Challenges We're Tackling Next

Enabling Production AI Access: You will partner closely with the Access & Identity platform to figure out how best to supply the structured schema and Knowledge Component APIs required to build a production-grade Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, paving the way for secure LLM integrations.

Taxonomy & Ontology Fluency: A strong, proven background in taxonomies, ontologies, and semantic content structuring.

Search & Content Discovery: A good understanding of modern search technologies, information retrieval, and content discovery, including how metadata, semantic search, and AI-powered capabilities improve content accessibility.

Senior IC Capabilities: Exceptional ability to lead by influence. You can confidently debate technical details with Principal Engineers while effectively communicating strategic value to commercial and editorial leadership.

sections.title: Role:
paras: We are seeking a Senior Product Manager to own verification and test management across the platform. That is the chain that runs from a requirement, to the test cases derived from it, to the runs that execute those cases, to the result a gate review accepts as evidence.

The scope covers hardware and software. On the hardware side the platform has to carry the DVP, test requests, sample and build allocation, lab and track capacity, and the DV and PV campaigns behind each program gate. On the software side it has to carry suites running in CI, on bench, on HIL, and in vehicle, tied to a release candidate and to the feature they verify.

The role is not the DVP owner and does not run tests. Test and Validation engineering does both, and will continue to. This will own the tooling they work in, the data model underneath it, and whether the coverage and evidence that come out of it survive a gate review. This is an internal product role, not a validation engineering role.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities:
bullets:
Capability Ownership: Verification and Test Management


• Own the strategy and roadmap for test case management and test run management as one connected capability, and carry that area into the platform roadmap.
Own the traceability model that links requirement to test case to test run to result to defect, and hold it steady as new programs, new variants, and new test types arrive
Sequence delivery against real vehicle program gates, and be able to state which gate a given scope or staffing decision causes us to make or miss

The Product Manager, Public Sector will lead Scale's product efforts across two connected focus areas — military planning and real-time AI and Alerting (LUX) — shaping real production outcomes and translating messy operational reality into high-signal input for the core platform.

This is not a roadmap PM, a CSM, or a solutions engineer. This PM owns product outcomes for a cross-cutting portfolio of AI and data capabilities: earning deep trust with senior military, civilian, and mission stakeholders, driving deployments to production inside classified and operationally constrained environments, identifying where the product is the bottleneck vs. execution, and feeding durable,…

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own product outcomes across Scale's military planning portfolio and/or its highest-impact national security accounts for LUX, spanning multiple DoW and National Security stakeholders and use cases. You are the accountable PM for product delivery and customer value.

Build trusted advisory relationships with senior military leaders (flag/general officer and senior civilian equivalents), National Security customer stakeholders, and senior technical leads. Become the reliable escalation point on the Scale side before issues surface externally.

Drive deployments from contract to production inside classified and operationally constrained environments — whether that means military planning workflows or LUX's low-latency, high-throughput, mission-critical data systems. You know what "production-ready" means inside DoW, and you close the gap.
Distinguish where the product is the constraint from where execution, integration, policy, or change management is the constraint. Drive each type of blocker to resolution through the right channel.
Shape a cross-cutting set of solutions spanning multiple stakeholders, echelons, and use cases, rather than owning a single point deployment.
Partner closely with Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) teams and Platform Capability teams so the account runs as a coordinated team, not a set of parallel workstreams.
Identify and develop expansion opportunities grounded in demonstrated customer value.
Represent customer reality to the platform and leadership with enough credibility that it changes decisions.

bullets: Enterprise deployment ownership : has driven AI/ML or complex/real-time software products from contract to production at scale — including near-zero-to-one, with no real users yet — with real integration, real security constraints, and real change management.

Domain fluency : working knowledge of the military planning process and modeling/simulation tools (e.g., Joint Planning Process, AFSIM), and/or the tradeoffs inherent to real-time, event-driven, high-throughput data architectures and their implications for AI agents — and how each shapes product decisions.
Product judgment in the field : translates customer reality into product direction, not just feature requests; can say no credibly and explain why.

Customer trust-building : earns and maintains trust with demanding senior military, civilian, and mission stakeholders over multi-quarter engagements; manages conflict without eroding the relationship.
Technical translation : bridges the gap between customer engineering/planning teams and Scale platform engineers; adds interpretation rather than simply relaying messages.

Operating in ambiguity and constrained environments : creates structure where there is none; makes decisions with incomplete information inside classified settings; does not wait for fully defined requirements.
Clear, precise communication : adjusts for audience (senior leader vs. engineer vs. PM); writes and speaks at the right level of detail; does not over- or under-explain.

bullets: Active TOP SECRET security clearance (TS/SCI eligibility preferred).
6+ years in product management, technical program management, or a customer-facing product ownership role
Direct experience working with the U.S. Department of War (DoW) or the broader U.S. national security community.
Working knowledge of at least one of the following, with an ability to speak credibly to the other:
The military planning process (e.g., the Joint Planning Process) and modeling/simulation systems (e.g., AFSIM).
Real-time streaming data systems — event-driven architectures, low-latency pipelines, and high-throughput data processing — and how they behave in production.

Demonstrated record of shipping AI or data products into large, constrained, classified, or highly regulated organizations — not pilots or proofs-of-concept. You can name the customer, the scale, the integration, and what production actually looked like.
Extreme ownership and follow-through: closes loops without reminders, drives outcomes across teams without formal authority, holds self and others to commitments.

You will collaborate broadly across the US Clinical Marketing, Global Product Marketing, US and Global Hospital Marketing, and Field Sales organizations to develop and execute marketing and sales strategies to drive adoption and utilization of advanced energy, stapling, and smart instrumentation in da Vinci procedures across surgical specialties.

sections.title: Roles & Responsibilities:
bullets: Engage key customers to accelerate technology adoption and utilization of all core product lines across surgical specialties.

Collect and consolidate Voice of Customer feedback to inform US Clinical Marketing, Global Product Marketing, and Sales Leadership teams of challenges and opportunities with current and newly launched products.
Identify and scale best demonstrated practices of Key Opinion Leaders and the Field Sales team to improve regional variation in technology adoption and utilization.
Identify and develop Product Champions for existing and newly launched products across surgical specialties.
Create clinical and economic reference stories to drive best demonstrated product choreographies and practices across surgical specialties and health systems.
Collaborate with Key Opinion Leaders, Global Product Marketing, and US Clinical Marketing to develop value propositions and messaging for new product launches.
Create and track key metrics of product adoption with US Sales Operations to leverage data that informs marketing and sales strategies and opportunities.
Develop and implement impactful training content for the Field Sales team with Commercial Learning that will accelerate technology adoption and utilization.

sections.title: Skills, Experience, Education, & Training:
paras:
• Excellent communication skills (written and verbal) and experience with presenting to surgeons and hospital executives.

• Previous surgical marketing experience in advanced energy or stapling of more than 2 years preferred.

• Previous surgical sales experience preferred, but not required.

• Minimum 8 years’ experience in a therapeutic or medical device company required.

• Surgical and/or Operating Room experience in sales or marketing required.

• Experience collaborating with Sales, Marketing Teams, Operations, and Customer Service required.

• Proven ability to effectively segment, target, position and message the product / procedure and develop strong sales support to drive product / procedure adoption.

• Demonstrated ability to work creatively, prioritize and smoothly manage goals and initiatives amidst competing priorities.

• Strong analytical capability and intuition required.

• Self-starter with the ability to problem solve and establish solutions in a high-growth and fast-paced environment.

• Superior verbal/written communication, teamwork, and interpersonal skills across multiple constituents.

• Strong knowledge of the Microsoft Office product suite.

• Ability to travel 50%, domestic.

sections.title: Minimum Education and Training Requirements:
paras:
• Bachelor’s degree required.

• MBA or other advanced degree preferred.

sections.title: Additional Information
paras: Due to the nature of our business and the role, please note that Intuitive and/or your customer(s) may require that you show current proof of vaccination against certain diseases including COVID-19. Details can vary by role.

smartrecruiters:servicenow:7440001513913.summary:
The Intelligent Services team is at the forefront of redefining how enterprises harness AI to deliver meaningful outcomes. Positioned within ServiceNow’s AI Innovation org, we build the connective tissue that powers enterprise search, agentic AI, and Intelligent workflows across the Now Platform. Our mission is to advance search and conversational AI capabilities that not only understand context but also anticipate user needs—unlocking new agentic opportunities, driving measurable value, and enabling real-time performance and CSAT insights.

Together, the Intelligent Services layer forms the foundation for Now Assist and agentic AI, giving ServiceNow a unique advantage in delivering AI that truly knows your business.

sections.title: The Impact You’ll Make:
paras: Intelligent Services is seeking a Senior Manager of Product Management for Search AI to lead the development of advanced enterprise search and conversational AI capabilities that enhance user experience and support the company's growth ambitions. This highly impactful, business-critical role is an opportunity to shape how search is employed to power richer, more intuitive conversational experiences. As the line between search and conversation blurs, you'll guide the development of our foundational search capabilities to create conversational experiences that are personalized, relevant, and grounded in trusted information. This manager will also lead a small team and integrate user insights to ensure customer-centric solutions.

sections.title: What you get to do in this role:
bullets: Set the vision for Enterprise Search & AI – Define and drive the product strategy for search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and question-answering capabilities that will power ServiceNow’s next wave of growth and innovation as we scale to $30B+ in revenue.
Own outcomes, not just outputs – Shape the product narrative, secure executive buy-in, and ensure every initiative delivers measurable business and customer impact.

Lead with technical depth and clarity – Guide engineering, ML research, UX research, and design partners with crisp, actionable requirements that enable fast, high-quality delivery of advanced search capabilities.
Champion user-driven innovation – Leverage customer pilots, user research, and market insights to create experiences that feel intuitive, contextual, and indispensable.
Drive adoption across the platform – Partner with other product teams to embed search and GenAI capabilities throughout the ecosystem, expanding their impact and value.
Measure what matters – Define and refine metrics that capture the real-world performance, relevance, and business value of search and AI features.
Develop future leaders – Manage and mentor a team of 4+ Product Managers, fostering a culture of innovation, accountability, and technical excellence.

sections.title: Qualifications
paras: We’re seeking a technical product leader with deep expertise in enterprise search and a passion for driving AI-powered innovation.

sections.title: The ideal candidate brings:
paras: For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $190,900 - $334,100 , plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.
bullets: Proven leadership: 10+ years building and leading high-performing product teams, including mentoring junior leaders and fostering cross-functional collaboration.
Enterprise Search expertise: 8+ years in software product management with hands-on experience building search or RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) products that drive measurable impact.

AI/ML fluency: Strong understanding of AI/ML frameworks and modern search technologies (e.g., Moveworks, Glean, Elasticsearch, Coveo), with the ability to evaluate, integrate, and innovate on emerging capabilities like context awareness, data indexing, and relevance ranking.
Execution excellence: A track record of delivering high-quality, scalable features at speed while maintaining a laser focus on outcomes that matter.
Customer obsession: Deep empathy for users and the ability to translate complex needs into elegant, customer-centric solutions.
Data-driven mindset: Expertise in leveraging qualitative and quantitative insights to validate hypotheses, guide strategy, and measure success.
Strategic problem-solving: Comfort navigating ambiguity, uncovering root problems, and clearly communicating trade-offs to drive decisions.

smartrecruiters:servicenow:7440001628268.summary: You are the primary relationship owner for a portfolio of accounts where the focus is helping customers adopt ServiceNow and realise the business value it delivers. You are accountable for adoption progress and customer success across your portfolio. This is a post-sales relationship role — you are the consistent presence the customer relies on, and the foundation from which strategic partnership is built. You can walk a customer through their success plan, identify risks before they escalate, and have a credible conversation about the value the platform is delivering. This role combines the orchestration and relationship management skills that keep customers on track, lead value conversations, and drive business outcomes.

sections.title: What you get to do in this role:
bullets: Hold clear accountability within your account portfolio — for adoption (entitlements, deployment,consumption and usage) and customer satisfaction

Build alignment and sponsorship with senior leaders in the customer. Understand the key stakeholders across IT, the business units and procurement, and the relevant partners; map them against ServiceNow's relationships, assess how strong each one is, and close the gap

Have value-led conversations with customer stakeholders at Director and VP level — able to articulate what the platform has delivered, what the next opportunity looks like, and beginning to shape how the customer thinks about their roadmap
Build and maintain success plans tied to customer business outcomes, agreeing value realisation measures with the customer and tracking progress against them

Drive adoption of AI and agentic capabilities on your accounts. Identify where customers are entitled but not yet deploying, and work with the account team to move them from entitlement to live use and measurable outcomes

Identify adoption and renewal risks early and act on them, using our standard risk process and securing approvals where needed. Manage escalations, engaging the right resources and driving the resolution plan to closure
Establish standard governance structures within ServiceNow teams and in partnership with the customer, so decisions have a clear path and accountability is driven towards a successful outcome

Advise and support customer implementations of ServiceNow — whether delivered by Expert Services, a ServiceNow partner or the customer's own team — so delivery stays aligned to the outcomes in the success plan

sections.title: To be successful in this role you have:
paras: For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $113,700 - $177,000 plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.
bullets: Experience in a customer-facing post-sales, consulting, or professional services role, with a track record of driving platform adoption and measurable customer outcomes. Exposure to technology-enabled transformation — AI, digital, SaaS, or enterprise software. ServiceNow knowledge, certification or training is a significant advantage

A minimum of 8 years in a management consulting or leadership role at a top-tier consulting firm, solution consulting, or similar positions focused on technology-enabled business transformations (Digital/SaaS/Enterprise Software)
Comfort with senior stakeholder conversations — typically Director and VP level in technology and the business, varying by account scale
A genuine interest in the customer's business, not just their platform — curious about their strategy, their pressures, and where they are trying to get to

A commercial mindset — able to spot expansion signals, but also to apply commercial logic to decisions: when requesting resources or investment, you understand the business case, expected outcome, cost, and P&L implications. You make commercially savvy recommendations, not just technically good ones
A working understanding of customer contracts — including term, renewal dates, product swaps—how to use them to protect and grow revenue
AI literacy — able to discuss how AI capability changes what the platform can do for a customer and what that means for their operating model
A working understanding of how software is delivered — including the software development lifecycle and Agile approaches such as Scrum — enough to advise on and support customer implementations

sections.title: Work Personas
paras: We approach our distributed world of work with flexibility and trust. Work personas (flexible, remote, or required in office) are categories that are assigned to ServiceNow employees depending on the nature of their work and their assigned work location. Learn more here . To determine eligibility for a work persona, ServiceNow may confirm the distance between your primary residence and the closest ServiceNow office using a third-party service.

sections.title: Export Control Regulations
paras: For positions requiring access to controlled technology subject to export control regulations, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), ServiceNow may be required to obtain export control approval from government authorities for certain individuals. All employment is contingent upon ServiceNow obtaining any export license or other approval that may be required by relevant export control authorities.

smartrecruiters:sgs:744000157623019.summary:
NOTE TO CANDIDATES - Candidates must reside in Maryland . Candidates with an analytical testing sales background are strongly encouraged to apply.

Own profitable growth and customer relationships for SGS Environmental Services across the Mid-Atlantic region. As an Environmental Senior Account Manager, you will develop new business, expand and retain existing accounts, and connect customers with environmental analytical services that support their project and compliance needs.

Your work will support customers addressing contaminated sites, water quality, and environmental risk. You will combine consultative selling, disciplined account management, responsive service, and technical collaboration to build long-term customer relationships.

sections.title: Job Description
paras: We are seeking a self-directed commercial professional who can translate customer needs into qualified opportunities, coordinate effectively across technical and operational teams, and maintain accountability from initial engagement through contract handoff.
This is an individual-contributor role with responsibility for building pipeline, achieving revenue targets, retaining assigned customers, and expanding SGS relationships across the territory.

sections.title: A day in the life of a SGS Senior Account Manager
paras:
You will connect customer needs with SGS capabilities, working closely with Client Services and laboratory operations to set clear expectations and support effective handoffs from sales to service delivery.

Job Functions
bullets: Develop and execute a territory and account plan that prioritizes new business, customer retention, account expansion, and profitable revenue growth.
Build and maintain a qualified pipeline through targeted prospecting, customer engagement, industry relationships, trade shows, and technical seminars.
Lead discovery conversations, assess customer requirements, and align opportunities with SGS capabilities, capacity, and service expectations.
Develop customer-specific value propositions and advance qualified opportunities through proposal, negotiation, and close.
Manage a portfolio of existing customers, identify expansion opportunities, and serve as the customer advocate within SGS.
Partner with Client Services, laboratory operations, technical experts, and other SGS business lines to coordinate solutions and deliver effective contract handoffs.
Maintain accurate account, activity, opportunity, next-step, and forecast information in the CRM and report progress against agreed performance measures.
Provide market and customer insights to support commercial plans, budgets, forecasts, sales materials, and service-development priorities.

sections.title: Required qualifications
bullets: Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, environmental science, or a related field.
At least five years of experience in technical sales, project management, customer service, or a related customer-facing role.
Demonstrated ability to develop customer relationships, identify needs, and advance commercial opportunities.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to collaborate effectively with customers and cross-functional teams.
Self-directed work style, sound commercial judgment, and the ability to prioritize resources and manage multiple opportunities.
Strong critical-thinking and quantitative skills, with the ability to assess customer requirements, solve problems, and interpret business information.
Advanced English-language proficiency.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.

sections.title: Preferred qualification
paras: This position pays $85,000 - $110,000 (dependent on experience) and is eligible for the EHS Sales commission plan. This position is not eligible for overtime pay.
In addition, your compensation package includes the following benefits:
bullets: At least five years of sales experience in the environmental industry, with preference for candidates who have Built Environment and Industrial Hygiene sales experience, including environmental analytical testing or related services.
Eligibility to participate in the Company’s benefit programs beginning on the first day of the month coinciding with or following the hire date.
Immediate eligibility to participate in the Company’s 401(k) Retirement Plan.
Paid vacation.
Four (4) floating holidays annually.
Seven (7) paid company-observed holidays.
Sick time accrual.
